blocks.body: To ensure thriving growth for Coffee Arabica starter plants, provide them with bright, indirect light to avoid leaf scorch or stunted growth. Maintain temperatures between 60-70°F (15-24°C) and high humidity levels of 50% or higher, misting the leaves or using a humidity tray if needed. Plant them in well-draining, slightly acidic soil with a pH of 6.0-6.5, and water when the top inch of soil dries out, keeping the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Fertilize every 2-4 weeks during the growing season with a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer like 10-10-10, or one slightly higher in nitrogen. Occasional pruning will encourage bushier growth, and repot the plant every 2-3 years to allow for healthy root expansion. Following these essentials will promote strong, vibrant Coffee Arabica plants.

# 1. Plant History

Coffee Arabica is native to the highlands of Ethiopia and Yemen. It is one of the most important coffee species in the world, accounting for about 60-70% of global coffee production. Cultivated for centuries, it is prized for its smoother flavor and lower caffeine content than other species.

Historically, Coffee Arabica beans were not brewed but mixed with fat and consumed by African tribes as an energy snack. Today, the seeds from its cherries are processed to produce the coffee beans that fuel the modern coffee industry.

![coffe ground.jpg](plant-img/coffee-arabica/coffe_ground.jpg)

# 2. General Description
Coffee Arabica (*Coffea arabica*).

![1.png](plant-img/coffee-arabica/1.png)

Coffee Arabica is a small evergreen shrub, reaching heights of up to 15 feet in the wild but can be pruned to remain a manageable indoor plant. It has glossy, dark green leaves and produces fragrant white flowers, followed by red or purple cherries that contain the seeds known as coffee beans.

Coffee Arabica produces small, white flowers that are intensely fragrant, reminiscent of jasmine. These flowers appear in clusters along the branches, usually after a rainy season. The blooming period typically lasts only a few days, but it is essential for fruit production. Once pollinated, the flowers give way to coffee cherries, which start green and mature to red or purple for 7 to 9 months. Though the flowering is brief, its success directly impacts the quality and quantity of the coffee harvest.

![coffee flower.jpg](plant-img/coffee-arabica/coffee_flower.jpg)

# 3. Care Requirement
Coffee Arabica thrives in USDA hardiness zones 9-11, where the warm temperatures are ideal for its growth.

![2.png](plant-img/coffee-arabica/2.png)

It prefers bright, indirect light, as too much direct sunlight can scorch the leaves, while insufficient light can stunt growth.
Water regularly, ensuring the soil remains consistently moist but not waterlogged. Let the top inch of soil dry before watering again.
High humidity (50% or more) is essential for healthy growth. Misting or placing the plant on a humidity tray helps maintain adequate moisture.
Coffee Arabica thrives in temperatures between 60-70°F (15-24°C) and should be protected from cold drafts and extreme heat.
The plant prefers well-draining soil with a slightly acidic pH of 6.0-6.5.

Feed every 2-4 weeks during the growing season with a balanced fertilizer like 10-10-10 to support healthy growth.

# 4. Maintenance Guide
Prune occasionally to maintain the desired size and encourage bushier growth. Remove any dead or yellowing leaves to keep the plant healthy.

Repot every 2-3 years to provide space for root expansion. Choose a slightly larger pot with fresh, well-draining soil.

# 5. Common Problems and Solutions
Coffee Arabica may attract pests like spider mites and aphids. Treat infestations with insecticidal soap or neem oil.
Overwatering can lead to root rot. Ensure proper drainage and avoid letting the plant sit in standing water.

Yellowing leaves can indicate overwatering or poor drainage, while scorched leaves point to too much direct sunlight.

# 6. Benefits and Uses

In addition to producing coffee beans, Coffee Arabica is an attractive houseplant with its glossy green leaves and fragrant flowers. It adds lush greenery to indoor spaces and outdoor gardens in warmer climates.

![3.png](plant-img/coffee-arabica/3.png)

# 7. Warnings or Precautions

Coffee Arabica contains caffeine, which can be toxic to pets if ingested. Keep the plant out of reach of animals.

# 8. Curiosities

Coffee Arabica beans develop more complex flavors when grown at higher altitudes, including notes of fruit, florals, and chocolate. These high-altitude beans are often used to make some of the world’s finest coffees.
